summary: TerraShift is an interactive web platform that uses NASA's GPM and MERRA-2 datasets to help users explore climate data, visualise environmental changes, and analyse trends through Guided and Expert modes using linear trend analysis and the Mann-Kendall statistical test, making Earth science more accessible to students, researchers, and the public while acknowledging that the developing prototype may still contain technical errors, limitations, and results requiring further validation.
details:
1. How It Works

  • Guided Mode: Step-by-step analysis designed for beginners.
  • Expert Mode: Greater control over data exploration and analysis.
  • Linear Trend Analysis: Identifies potential long-term trends.
  • Mann-Kendall Test: Evaluates potential monotonic trends in environmental data.
  • Interactive visualisations help users interpret complex datasets.

2. Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Makes NASA Earth science data more accessible.
  • Reduces barriers to climate data analysis.
  • Encourages scientific curiosity, data literacy, and environmental awareness.
  • Supports students, educators, researchers, and the public in understanding environmental changes.

3. Technologies and Tools

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript
  • 3D Visualisation: Three.js
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI
  • NASA Data: GPM IMERG, MERRA-2 via NASA GES DISC
  • Deployment: Vercel,Render
  • AI Development Assistance: Kiro, ChatGPT

4. Creativity and Design Considerations

  • Combines scientific analysis with interactive visualisation and accessible learning.
  • Integrates data exploration, statistical analysis, and visual interpretation.
  • Considers beginner accessibility, usability, dataset complexity, and analytical reliability for student

5. Limitations and Future Improvements

  • TerraShift is currently a developing prototype.
  • Some technical errors, incomplete features, or unexpected results may remain.For example, data cannot be reach, Location not showing, long loading progress.
  • Further testing, debugging, and scientific validation are needed.
  • Future improvements aim to enhance reliability, accuracy, usability, and analytical capabilities.
